blocks.label: POST 08'S WINDOW
blocks.text: Shrinking only lowers the total when every number is [[positive]]. A −1 can make it go up.
Running sums don't care about signs: any two that are k apart mark a subarray.

blog.summary: Count subarrays that add up to k, even with negative numbers: remember how often each running sum appeared.
blog.tested_inputs: hand-picked cases (k = 0, all zeros, sums that cancel out, one value) and random arrays of up to 14 numbers from −5 to 5 with random k, plus one array of 2,000 numbers
blog.tested_against: a brute force that adds up every subarray
blog.tested_extra: The running sums, the count for k = 3 and k = 4 and the trap result come from running the code.

caption.first: LeetCode 560 Subarray Sum Equals K: running sums plus a hash map count subarrays in one pass, negatives included.
lines: At each number, add how many earlier running sums equal sum − k.
The trap: forget seen[0] = 1 and 1 −1 3 1 2 gives 3 instead of 4.
